summary:
Iter39 — Crossword UI overhaul + Daily difficulty bump regression. ALL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA PASS.

Backend (15/15 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_iter39_crossword_daily_difficulty.py, ~3s):
• GET /api/games/crossword/daily now returns a HARD or EXPERT puzzle (verified live: today's daily = expert-006 "Aussie TV Classics"). Points envelope = 30 (expert 25 + daily bonus 5); also asserts points=20 for hard. Theme is NOT in the previous MEDIUM theme set ("Aussie Slang", "Around the House", etc.).
• Daily envelope contains `date` (today UTC ISO), `discussion_table_id` (string), and `puzzle` with no `answer` leak in any clue.
• /api/games/crossword/levels still lists all 4 levels (easy/medium/hard/expert), and /api/games/crossword/active/{level} returns puzzles for every level — the library is intact, only the daily picker changed.
• Single-puzzle GET (/api/games/crossword/{id}) still works for easy/medium/hard/expert ids with answers stripped.
• POST /api/games/crossword/{id}/check still returns the `solved` + `status` grid (empty grid → solved=false, blocked cells correctly tagged).
• GET /api/games/crossword/{id}/reveal/{r}/{c} (the "hint" endpoint per the brief) still returns the correct letter.
• The Coffee Lounge "Today's Crossword" table (surfaced via GET /api/tables, filtered by discussion_table_id) now has the tougher description copy — contains the substring "tough" or "brain-teaser" per the new _ensure_daily_crossword_table() rewrite.

Frontend (Playwright, mobile 390×844 + tablet 1024×768 against /games/crossword/play?daily=1):
PHONE (stacked layout):
  • `[data-testid="crossword-clue-panel-stacked"]` present, `crossword-clue-panel-wide` absent.
  • Dense grid renders (`Aussie TV Classics`, today's daily — screenshot confirmed).
  • Active-clue banner appears below the grid with `Previous clue` + `Next clue` accessibility-labelled buttons (1 of each found).
  • `ACROSS (4)` section header present with 4 clue rows, `DOWN (7)` section present with 7 clue rows.
  • Tapping a Down clue row updates the banner heading from `3 ACROSS · 11 letters` → `1 DOWN · 16 letters` (clue picker integration working).
  • Timer pill: initial state shows the live counter (e.g. `0:05`) with accessibilityLabel="Hide timer". Tap → label becomes "Timer" and the eye-off icon is used (Show timer accessibility label present). Tap again → live counter restored (Hide timer accessibility label back).
TABLET (side-by-side layout):
  • `[data-testid="crossword-clue-panel-wide"]` present, stacked absent.
  • Layout flips correctly — screenshot confirms grid on the left + bordered scrollable clue panel on the right with `ACROSS (4)` highlighted-first-clue visible in teal background + left-border accent (Summer Bay soap, run together) and `DOWN (7)` rendered below.
  • Clue rows are tappable (4 across rows found, tap invoked). Note: React Native Web does NOT propagate `accessibilityState.selected: true` to the DOM as `aria-selected="true"`, so I couldn't verify the new selection state via aria; the visual highlight (background colour + left border accent + bold font) is the source of truth and is clearly working in the screenshot.

Known stale test flagged for E1: /app/backend/tests/test_iter37_crossword.py::TestDaily::test_daily_puzzle_envelope still hard-codes `p["level"] == "medium"` and `d["points"] == 15` — that test will now FAIL because daily is hard/expert. It needs to be updated to allow {hard, expert} and 20/30 points (or be superseded by the new iter39 file). I did NOT modify iter37 — change is intentional per the brief, the test file just needs an update.

minor.issue: Stale test — asserts daily level=='medium' and points==15. Needs update to allow level in ('hard','expert') and points in (20, 30) after the iter39 difficulty bump. Not a backend bug — a test fixture that drifted with intended behaviour.

react_native_issues.issue: React Native Web deprecation warnings persisting in browser console — `shadow*` style props (use boxShadow), `textShadow*` (use textShadow), `props.pointerEvents` (use style.pointerEvents), `Animated useNativeDriver` warning. Not introduced by iter39 — same warnings flagged in iter37/38.

`accessibilityState={{ selected: isActive }}` does NOT render as `aria-selected="true"` in React Native Web (only role="button" reaches the DOM). The visual highlight works fine, but the selected-state is not exposed to assistive tech / Playwright via aria. Consider adding `testID` to each clue row (e.g. `crossword-clue-A-3` / `crossword-clue-D-1`) so testing + screen readers can deterministically identify the active row.

action_items: Update /app/backend/tests/test_iter37_crossword.py::TestDaily::test_daily_puzzle_envelope to expect level in ('hard','expert') and points in (20, 30) — or delete it in favour of iter39's TestDailyDifficulty class which covers the same envelope assertions with the new contract.

(Polish) Add `testID` attributes to crossword clue rows in CluePanel (play.tsx:783) so the active row can be deterministically identified during testing and by screen readers — RN Web does NOT translate `accessibilityState.selected` to `aria-selected` in the DOM.

(Polish) Add `testID="crossword-timer-pill"` to the timer Pressable in play.tsx:441 — currently the only handle is accessibilityLabel which switches between 'Hide timer' / 'Show timer', making tests dependent on the current toggle state.

(Pre-existing, not introduced by iter39) Address React Native Web deprecation warnings: replace `shadow*`/`textShadow*` props with `boxShadow`/`textShadow`, move `pointerEvents` to style, and audit `Animated.useNativeDriver` usage on web.
critical_code_review_comments: crossword_puzzles.py:756 daily_puzzle() concatenates HARD_PUZZLES + EXPERT_PUZZLES into a fresh `pool` list every call — fine for correctness, but mildly wasteful. Could be a module-level constant `DAILY_POOL = HARD_PUZZLES + EXPERT_PUZZLES` computed once.

crossword_puzzles.py:770 fallback when both HARD/EXPERT pools are empty silently switches to MEDIUM with a comment — good safety net, but worth a `log.warning()` so a deploy with truncated puzzle lists is noisy in Sentry rather than silently regressing the difficulty bump.

play.tsx:756 CluePanel auto-scroll uses `useEffect` keyed off `activeKey` and reads `offsets.current.get(...)` — fine, but if the active clue is the FIRST one in its section and its onLayout fires AFTER the first render (race), the initial scroll-to-top happens before the offset is known. Today the panel starts at y=0 so this is invisible, but if the parent ever adds a header above the panel the first auto-scroll could overshoot. Consider falling back to scrollIntoView via measureInWindow or stamping the y with a ref+state on first measure.

play.tsx:573 active-clue banner uses `c.brandTertiary` background with `c.brand` border + `c.onSurface` text — visually clean, but the `21 * scale` font is the only text the user reads while typing. Could benefit from explicit minimum tap target on Prev/Next (already 48px via styles.navBtn — good).

play.tsx:825 the wide-layout ScrollView has `maxHeight: panelMaxHeight` but no minHeight — on very-tall tablets the panel could collapse if the grid renders shorter than expected. Probably fine in practice, just worth a sanity check on iPad Pro landscape.

seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Tests use maggie's demo session for any user-scoped endpoints; iter37 conftest pattern not needed here because all 15 iter39 tests are read-only (GET) or stateless POSTs (check with empty/wrong grid). No data persisted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend env var key is EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (frontend/.env). Crossword endpoints actually deployed: GET /levels, /daily, /active/{level}, /{puzzle_id}, /{puzzle_id}/reveal/{r}/{c}, POST /{puzzle_id}/check, POST/GET /progress/{user_id}. The brief mentioned `/puzzles`, `/puzzle/{id}`, `/check`, `/hint` — those are aliases for /active/{level}, /{puzzle_id}, /{puzzle_id}/check, /{puzzle_id}/reveal respectively (the brief's names don't literally exist as routes). FE testIDs available on the crossword play screen: crossword-clue-panel-stacked (phone) and crossword-clue-panel-wide (tablet). Timer pill + Prev/Next buttons + clue rows have NO testIDs yet — they're locatable via accessibilityLabel ("Hide timer"/"Show timer", "Previous clue"/"Next clue", and "Across N: <clue>" / "Down N: <clue>" patterns). React Native Web does NOT propagate accessibilityState.selected as aria-selected, so use the visual styling (left border + brandTertiary background) to verify the active clue, or add testIDs per the action items. Today's daily (2026-06-23) is expert-006 "Aussie TV Classics" — daily_puzzle() uses (today_utc - 2026-01-01).days % len(HARD+EXPERT pool) to rotate, so each calendar day picks a different puzzle. Note: /app/backend/tests/test_iter37_crossword.py::TestDaily::test_daily_puzzle_envelope is STALE post-iter39 and will fail any regression run until updated — flagged in action_items.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all iter39 acceptance criteria pass. Only nit: the previous iter37 daily envelope test is now stale (asserts medium/15) and needs a one-line update to allow {hard,expert}/{20,30}. The new iter39 test file supersedes that assertion.
